text:
devon: heads-up — CI is red on the paged+flashattn variant again, looks toolchain-related this time. repros locally in a container that differs from the CI image.

mike_t: can you paste the failing link step?

devon: sure. short log: 
```
/usr/bin/ld: /root/.cache/pip-wheel.../libflashattn.a(paged_kernels.o): in function `paged_attention::compute':
paged_kernels.cu:(.text+0x2f4): undefined reference to `__cuda_something'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

sara: classic mismatch between the host nvcc+gcc combo and the base image libs. CI uses gcc13 on bookworm image; local dev container is gcc12/bullseye.

luis: also saw this crop up when we switched the FlashAttention flavor to enable fused kernels — symbol names changed slightly and some inline asm expects different abi.

devon: interestingly, when I build with `-DNO_FUSED_ATTENTION` the link passes. with fused on it fails.

mike_t: could be C++ ABI or visibility flags. try adding `-fvisibility=hidden -fPIC -fno-semantic-interposition` to the compile flags for the fused object and see whether the unresolved symbol goes away.

devon: tried `-fno-semantic-interposition` locally — link succeeds, but runtime perf for small prompt batches regresses 8-12%. profiling shows extra indirections in the fused kernel path.

sara: do you have the profiler output? flamegraph?

devon: posted a short perf snippet: 
```
baseline (paged, no fused): median latency p50=18.3ms, p95=42.7ms, tokens/sec=480
fused-on + local flags: p50=19.9ms, p95=48.1ms, tokens/sec=435
fused-on + -fno-semantic-interposition: p50=20.6ms, p95=50.2ms, tokens/sec=410
kv cache thrash observed: extra memcpy calls up 2.3x when sequence split hits new page boundary
```

luis: kv cache thrash is worrying — could be our batching heuristics crossing page boundaries more often with fused kernels (different block sizes). that would explain memcpys.

ops-bot: <deploy-job:  /job/infra/flashattn-paged/build/4412> failed step linking-flashattn (exit code 1)

mike_t: two action items: 1) add gcc12/13 matrix to the linux-builder CI for the paged+fused job, 2) add a lightweight perf test that simulates small-batch user traces (seq len mix) to catch kv thrash regressions automatically.

sara: I'll file a short RFC that proposes: matrix + an opt-in env var in CI to toggle `-fno-semantic-interposition` and run perf smoke. also propose we pin the docker base to bookworm consistently for that job.

devon: append tests: local reproducer command I used: 
```
docker run -it --rm -v $(pwd):/src redwood/build:dev-bookworm bash -c "cd /src && python -m build && pip install dist/*.whl && pytest tests/integration/test_paged_attention.py::test_small_batch_trace -q"
```
That reproduces the linker failure when using the bullseye-based dev image.

luis: quick mitigation: we'll revert the fused-default flip in the model catalog for Dedicated until CI matrix added. do we need a rollback PR?

mike_t: yes, revert toggle in prod config + add canary that points a small % of traffic to fused variant behind a perf monitor.

devon: noted. I'll open the revert PR and the CI matrix ticket. tagging @mike_t @sara for follow-ups. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: created issue #4789: "CI: add gcc12/13 + bookworm matrix for paged+fused flashattn"

sara: thanks — let's keep the perf smoke in CI fast (<= 90s). small-batch synthetic trace should be enough to catch the memcpy/kv thrash.

mike_t: awesome. one more: add a BUILD_TAG in the artifact name that records the compiler+libc combo so we can correlate artifacts with regressions.

devon: agreed. I'll include that in the PR.

luis: ping me when the revert PR is up; I'll coordinate the deploy and the canary config.

devon: done for now, will follow up with links in the PR thread.
